{{Quote|Alzoc wasn't even entered in the galactic registry. The Senate found a mention of it a couple of years ago in secret corporate files. Nobody knew what was going on there. They were lied to, betrayed…no wonder they learned to distrust anything humanoid.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="COJnote">This date is based on the stationing of stormtroopers on the planet for the ''Eye of Palpatine'' mission. In [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], set 12 ABY, Triv Pothman had been on Pzob for 30 years. Presuming the Alzoc III contingent was stationed there at a similar time, the planet must have been discovered by 18 BBY.</ref>}}
'''Alzoc III''' was the third [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Alzoc system/Legends|Alzoc system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was a frozen planet, dominated by arctic tundra and frozen wastes. This limited the amount of wildlife on the surface. The sole [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the planet was the [[Talz/Legends|Talz]]. Tall bipeds covered in gray-white fur, they were notable for their four [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], an adaptation to dazzling sunlight reflected off snow.

While the planet was sporadically visited during the reign of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], its major introduction to galactic society was through [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]]. Discovering a world rich with natural resources and an available work force, the Empire secretly enslaved the planet, conscripting the natives to work in large mines. The extracted [[Ore/Legends|ore]] was then shipped off to Imperial shipyards; the valuable [[Alzoc pearl]] was also collected. The Empire only withdrew from the planet after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] as part of widespread consolidation of forces. The New Republic later discovered records of the planet and established contact.

The planet was twice revisited by Imperial elements in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]]. The ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'', a rogue battlemoon, stopped there to collect long-absent stormtroopers, before continuing on to [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]]. That year, the [[Empire Reborn]] also established a base on the planet, which was infiltrated by [[New Republic Intelligence Service]] agents [[Kyle Katarn]] and [[Jan Ors]].

==Description==
{{Quote|On Alzoc…ah, there is the finest of nectar to sip!|[[Muftak/Legends|Muftak]] dreams of Alzoc III|<ref name="TME">{{StoryCite|story=Play It Again, Figrin D'an: The Tale of Muftak and Kabe|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
Alzoc III was a frozen planet, with snow and ice dominating its surface. It was covered in vast frozen wastelands, bisected by a number of deep valleys<ref name="EGtPM" /> and mountain ranges.<ref name="JKJO" /> Frigid gales swept the planet,<ref name="TBSB">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref> often resulting in snow storms. The [[Valley of Blizzards]] was particularly notable for this phenomenon.<ref name="EGtPM" /> A number of frozen lakes also covered the surface.<ref name="EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref> During the daylight hours, sunlight reflected from the snow fields could be blinding, capable of burning the retinas of many [[Species/Legends|species]]. Nights on the moonless planet reached the other extreme, blanketed in darkness.<ref name="GG4" />

[[File:AlzocIIITrees.jpg|thumb|left|Sparse foliage on Alzoc III]]
Aside from the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] Talz, there was virtually no wildlife on the planet. The [[snow slug]] was the only species readily visible on the planet's surface;<ref name="FOC" /> a slug with large teeth, it plowed through the snowfields with its mouth open, catching prey in its cave-like mouth and leaving a trail of melted snow in its wake.<ref name="EGtPM" /> Imperial bioengineers considered using the snow slug as part of an experiment to create bioweapons, but the project produced no results.<ref name="ROD">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Ruins of Dantooine]]''</ref> A second animal native to Alzoc was the [[torsk]]. The [[t'landa Til]] [[Teroenza]] was known to possess a sculpture of a torsk carved from [[Lapis/Legends|lapis]].<ref name="TPS" /> During the Imperial occupation of the planet, [[Shaak/Legends|shaak]] were introduced to the planet as livestock. They were reared by a [[Alzoc III Food Commissioner|Food Commissioner]] who managed supplies on the planet.<ref name="FOC" />

Flora on the planet included a species of [[Tree/Legends|fir tree]] that grew sparsely over the planet.<ref name="EAW" /> The orphan [[Muftak/Legends|Muftak]], born on the desert world of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], had recurring dreams of his homeworld which he believed to be a form of genetic memories. These dream-memories contained images of rich and lush jungles, with huge bell-shaped flowers of all colors hanging from the foliage. Within the depths of these flowers, reservoirs of rich nectar formed. In his dreams, this liquid was full of marvelous rippling flavors, drunk by the Talz through their proboscis. While these dream-memories did not correlate to the environment of Alzoc III during his lifetime, it is possible they reflected an earlier period in the planet's history.<ref name="TME" />

==History==
===Pre-Imperial era===
{{Quote|Everyone knows the deficiencies in the Registry's information. And the Empire "protected the rights" of Alzoc III, of Garnib, of Trosh…|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]|<ref name="PoT">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>}}
Around [[30,000 BBY]], the planet was ruled by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] which dominated much of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] through their interstellar [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].<ref name="TEA" /> During this time, the creature known as [[Gharj]] was unleashed on the native [[Talz/Legends|Talz]], leading the Talz to worship the beast and its Rakatan masters.<ref name="Eternity">{{TORcite|type=operation|Eternity Vault}}</ref> With the collapse of the Empire five thousand years later, the Rakatans retreated to their homeworld, leaving little trace as to how and why they left.<ref name="TEA" />

A Talz was sighted off-world as early as [[3993 BBY]] on the planet [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="S&L">{{Tales|23|Shadows and Light}}</ref> During this same period, a Talz worked as a member of the [[Jedi Covenant]]'s [[Covenant Shadow|Shadows]].<ref name="kotor25">[[Knights of the Old Republic 25|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 25]]</ref> During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] just over three centuries later, many Talz joined the Republic's military efforts on the frigid planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]],<ref name="Talz Codex">{{TORcite|type=codex|Talz}}</ref> and near the end of the Cold War Alzoc III and the [[Sujimis sector/Legends|Sujimis sector]] were represented in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] by [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Tal Teff]].<ref name="Duel">{{TORcite|type=class|Smuggler|The Duel|Alderaan}}</ref> The world was also visited by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] as part of their early reconnaissance around [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]]; a number of the natives were taken captive for experimentation by the extra-galactic invaders.<ref name="AOC">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial]]''</ref> Prior to the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], some Talz lived and traveled off-world, with individuals living on [[Maramere]],<ref name="SC">''[[Star Wars: Starfighter: Crossbones]]''</ref> [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]],<ref name="G7">{{GamerCite|7|Reckonings}}</ref> [[Questal/Legends|Questal]],<ref name="GCQ">''[[The Game Chambers of Questal]]''</ref> and [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]], where [[Bama Vook]] worked as a test pilot for [[Trinkatta Starships]].<ref name="E1A2">''[[Episode I Adventures 2: The Bartokk Assassins]]''</ref> A sizable community of Talz also lived on [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]], coming into conflict with the [[Pantoran/Legends|Pantorans]] from the orbiting moon.<ref name="Trespass">{{TCW|Trespass}}</ref> Perhaps the most notable off-world Talz during this period was the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Foul Moudama]], though few knew of his origins. He fought as a [[General/Legends|General]] in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and was killed while protecting the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]].<ref name="CW">{{DB|character|foulmoudama|Moudama, Foul}}</ref>

[[File:SecuraUnduliVsVentress-TCWRH.jpg|thumb|right|Aayla Secura and Luminara Unduli engage Asajj Ventress while on a mission during the Clone Wars.]]
During the Clone Wars, the planet was considered to be in territory controlled by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. Following the [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|Battle of Ryloth]], Alzoc temporarily became a point of interest for both sides of the conflict. The [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] had stolen a [[Gravitic Core]] from a [[Munificent-class star frigate/Legends|Munificent-class star frigate]] in orbit above the planet, leaving the ship to be destroyed by an explosion of the other core it was carrying. The core was to be used in a new [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Gravitic polarization beam|superweapon]], designed to have enough power to collapse a star. The frigate crashed on Alzoc, where the gravitic core created a gravity anomaly, causing the ship's wreckage to float in the air near the crash site alongside ice debris. Shortly thereafter, Jabba informed the Republic of CIS activity near the planet, hoping to punish the Separatists for passing through his territory without payment. The [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] soon dispatched [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] and [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] to investigate the report.<ref name="TCW:RH">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Republic Heroes]]''</ref>

Accompanied by a detachment of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] led by commanders [[Bly/Legends|CC-5052]] and [[Gree (clone trooper)/Legends|CC-1004]], the two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] arrived at Alzoc, dispatching several [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TEs]] to the planet's surface. However, by that time the crash site was already being visited by the Confederate [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolyte]] of [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. In order to keep the new gravitic weapon a secret, Dooku ordered his agent to destroy any evidence of the incident and allow no witness to be left alive. When the Republic forces arrived at the crash site, both Jedi and the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] were stunned by the view of huge masses of ice and numerous starship parts floating freely in the air and decided to investigate the vessel. They were engaged by many [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] dispatched by Ventress to keep the Jedi occupied, while she went about setting the remains of the ship for self-destruct in order to destroy all evidence of the new superweapon's existence and eliminate the Republic forces. After finding the ship's data recorder, Secura and Unduli were able to uncover a record of the ship's last moments, as well as access the ship's manifest, learning about the existence of the gravitic weapon. After narrowly escaping the ship before it exploded, the Jedi were ambushed by the [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] assassin. After a brief duel, the two Jedi Masters overpowered the Dark Acolyte, trapping her under a bulk of ice. Unduli then ordered the clones to make contact with [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to report the results of their mission to the Jedi Council. The discovery of the new weapon later helped the Republic destroy the CIS superweapon in a battle on [[Behpour/Legends|Behpour]].<ref name="TCW:RH" />

===Galactic Empire era===
[[File:ColdHandsWarmGun-JODemo.png|thumb|left|The Imperial base on Alzoc III]]
While Imperial [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] discovered the planet sometime before [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="COJnote">This date is based on the stationing of stormtroopers on the planet for the ''Eye of Palpatine'' mission. In [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], set 12 ABY, Triv Pothman had been on Pzob for 30 years. Presuming the Alzoc III contingent was stationed there at a similar time, the planet must have been discovered by 18 BBY.</ref> they found that the majority of the Talz were unaware of galactic civilization. Their society was a primitive one, making use of simple tools to build shelters from the cold. Realizing the potential untapped labor force represented by the Talz, the discovery was never listed on the [[Galactic Registry]], in order to circumvent Senate regulations regarding the treatment of primitive peoples.<ref name="UAA" /> Instead the Empire enslaved the species, with the indirect aid of the professional [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] slaver [[Borun Call]].<ref name="AJ10">{{JournalCite|10|Wanted by Cracken (Star Wars Adventure Journal)}}. No details of Borun Call's involvement are given.</ref> They then set up huge mines, putting the Talz to work in unforgiving conditions. In addition to [[Ore/Legends|ores]] shipped off to major shipyards, Imperials also found valuable [[Alzoc pearl]]s on the planet.<ref name="TAB">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> [[Obo Rin]], an Imperial [[sentientologist]], characterized their presence as protective, citing the need to prevent offworlders enslaving the primitive species. In actuality, the Empire kept the planet off limits and banned the Talz from leaving their world in order to keep a monopoly on this resource. To further this end, the Empire offered a 5,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] bounty for the capture or execution of any Talz found offworld.<ref name="GG4" />

The Talz suffered greatly under Imperial occupation and were worked to death in the mines with minimum rations. This situation was alleviated for a short period under the supervision of Imperial officer [[Pter Thanas]]. Calculating that overall efficiency would increase if the Talz were supplied more food, he increased their food allotment. Profits did improve, and the Talz returned his generosity by saving his life when he almost fell down the mines. However, six months later, his reforms were reversed by a new [[Colonel/Legends|colonel]]. When a Talz headman asked for a return to the additional rations, the colonel ordered his village destroyed. Despite Thanas's refusal, the village was destroyed, and Thanas was shipped off to [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]] for his impertinence.<ref name="TBSB" />

[[File:AlzocSurface.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An AT-ST on patrols on Alzoc III.]]
Despite their best efforts to keep Alzoc III isolated from the galaxy, the Imperials were not entirely successful. The criminal [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] became aware of the planet and attempted to extort the Imperial Food Commissioner there, in order to gain access to the planet's profits.<ref name="FOC" /> A number of Talz also escaped the planet, finding refuge in fringe communities such as the [[Artists' High Commune]] on [[Mrlssi]],<ref name="XW">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: The Phantom Affair]]''</ref> on frontier worlds such as [[Feriae Junction/Legends|Feriae Junction]]<ref name="M27">[[Star Wars (1977) 27|''Star Wars'' (1977) 27]]</ref> [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]<ref name="Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> and [[Tandankin]],<ref name="Apple">''[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron Special]]''</ref> or by taking advantage of Imperial-free zones such as [[The Wheel/Legends|The Wheel]] casino<ref name="M19">[[Star Wars (1977) 19|''Star Wars'' (1977) 19]]</ref> and [[Void Station]].<ref name="IA">''[[Star Wars: Empire: Idiot's Array]]''</ref> Not all the escaped Talz chose to lay low, some choosing instead to fight the Galactic Empire. One joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] as a fighter pilot in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="XW:WS">''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]''</ref> while another sought to bring rebellion to his home world. He managed to convince a group of adventurers to return with him to Alzoc III and lead a revolt. Those he recruited had to contend not only with the Imperial presence, but also with Talz collaborators; some of the natives chose to work with the Imperials in keeping their species under control, in exchange for special favors. [[Gar (Talz)|Gar]], in particular, resisted the adventurers attempts at insurgency.<ref name="GMS">''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Screen]]''s''. This is based on an adventure seed.</ref> While this attempted revolution was ultimately unsuccessful, the Talz finally got their freedom shortly after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]; due to the massive defeat there, Imperial leaders consolidated their forces throughout the galaxy, withdrawing them from many [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] holdings, including Alzoc III.<ref name="EGtPM" />

===New Republic era===
It was not until [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]] that the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] discovered mention of the planet in secret corporate files.<ref name="NRdiscovery">In [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Luke Skywalker states that the Senate found mention of Alzoc III "a couple of years ago", placing it around 10 ABY. However, in ''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]'' Wedge Antilles knew of the planet while recruiting pilots for Wraith Squadron. This novel is set in 7 ABY, slightly earlier than the date suggested by Luke Skywalker, but this year is used as Luke statement is loose. The New Republic Senate was founded in 7 ABY so this date is consistent.</ref> Rediscovering the planet, the New Republic introduced the Talz to many other species. Mining continued on the planet under New Republic supervision,<ref name="UAA" /> with the Talz taking ownership of the mines. They began to develop a system of trade with offworlders, although they interacted with their trading partners guardedly. Talz leaving their world was still rare during this period, although some did so.<ref name="EGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> Some of these travelers were captured by the Imperial warlord [[Zsinj]] for use in his experiments. His scientists pumped the beings full of chemicals in order to stimulate their rage centers. One such individual was released by [[Castin Donn]] and killed a number of his tormentors before being killed himself.<ref name="XW:IF">''[[X-Wing: Iron Fist]]''</ref>

In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], the planet was visited by the ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'', an Imperial battlemoon, which had been dormant for 30 years. Originally commissioned by [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] in order to destroy a Jedi enclave on [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]], the battlemoon had been disabled by the Jedi Knight [[Callista Ming]] before it could be activated. When it was restarted by the dark Jedi [[Irek Ismaren]], it carried out its programming written years earlier, which included clandestinely gathering an aggregate of two stormtrooper companies from a number of Outer Rim worlds where they had been stationed decades earlier. Unable to find the long absent stormtroopers,<ref name="COJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> the slowly deteriorating [[DZ-70 fugitive tracker droid]]s of the ''Eye of Palpatine'' took aboard whatever bipeds they could find.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> As such, when it stopped at Alzoc III, it took a number of Talz aboard, attempting to indoctrinate them as stormtroopers. The battlemoon was prevented from completing its mission by the Jedi Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and two of his trainees, who had also been conscripted by the starship while stranded on [[Pzob/Legends|Pzob]]. Skywalker managed to evacuate all the inhabitants off the starship, with aid from the Talz, before one of his companions self-destructed it. Skywalker later ensured the Talz were returned to Alzoc III.<ref name="COJ" />

[[File:Talz_village.png|thumb|left|200px|A Talz village near the Valley of Blizzards.]]
The ice planet was again visited by Imperial-aligned forces when the [[Empire Reborn]], a splinter movement, established a small outpost there. The movement was led by former [[Procurator of Justice]], Lord [[Hethrir]], who while in office had overseen extensive slaving operations throughout the galaxy. It is possible that it was in this capacity that he established a presence on the ice planet. Rumors of the Imperial activities there reached [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], head of the [[New Republic Intelligence Service]]. She hired the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] [[Kyle Katarn]] and [[Jan Ors]] to [[Mission at Alzoc III (Empire Reborn)|investigate]]; posing as cargo haulers delivering goods in their starship, the ''[[Raven's Claw]]'', Katarn infiltrated the base from within one of the cargo containers. However, the Imperial forces became aware of his activity, and took Ors captive; she had landed the ''Raven's Claw'' in another hangar bay to wait for Kyle. Despite the outpost being defended by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]], and [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]-wielding members of the [[Reborn]]—warriors artificially imbued with [[The Force/Legends|The Force]]—Katarn, a former Jedi himself, was able to rescue Ors and escape the base.<ref name="JKJO" />

As Alzoc III became more established in the galaxy, new opportunities opened up for the Talz. One youngling went on to train at the [[Jedi Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] among such Jedi luminaries as [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Lowbacca]].<ref name="YJK">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Heirs of the Force]]''</ref> [[Aj Koenes]] would train as a water specialist, later working for the [[Senate Select Committee for Refugees]] (SELCORE) in terraforming [[Duro/Legends|Duro]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="BP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref> Talz also traveled to worlds such as [[Phaeda/Legends|Phaeda]],<ref name="CE">''[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire]]''</ref> [[Vaynai/Legends|Vaynai]],<ref name="VA">{{GamerCite|8|The Vaynai Archipelago}}</ref> and [[Lok/Legends|Lok]].<ref name="L">[[Legacy (2006) 2|''Legacy'' (2006) 2]]</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|The Talz home planet. Alzoc Three is calm, icy, peaceful. Everything we hate.|[[Broonmark]]|<ref name="Broonmark">{{TORcite|type=conversation|[[Broonmark]]|Clan Vengeance}}</ref>}}
[[File:Two_Talz.png|thumb|right|Two native Talz]]
The sole sentient species of Alzoc III was the Talz, tall fur covered bipeds. Averaging 2 meters in height, the species was very strong, and this, combined with the large claws on their hands, made them appear fierce to other species. The Talz were well adapted to their planet, with a thick covering of white and gray fur to insulate them from the cold. Their most distinctive feature was the four [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] on their head. This too, was an adaptation to their planet. The smaller pair was used during the day when sunlight reflected intensely off the snowfields. The larger pair was reserved for the deep darkness of night, when the moonless sky supplied virtually no light. A small proboscis extended from underneath their eyes.<ref name="GG4" />

Despite their fearsome appearance, the Talz were peaceful individuals. Their irenic nature made them particularly pliable to Imperial control. Acting counter to their nature caused high levels of stress, often resulting in psychosomatic illnesses.<ref name="XW:WS" /> Talz society revolved around extensive family and extended family ties, which ensured resources were redistributed to ensure the wider good.<ref name="GG4" /> They spoke the [[Language/Legends|language]] [[Talz (language)|Talz]], and when later introduced to galactic society could understand [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], but were unable to speak it due to the shape of their proboscis.<ref name="UAA" /> This inability could be overcome by the use of [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulators]]<ref name="E1A2" /> or [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]].<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

==Locations==
===Alzoc III mines===
{{Main|Alzoc III mines}}
The Galactic Empire established huge mines on Alzoc III in order to extract the vast virgin ore deposits on the planet. The open pits bored deeply through the red rocky soil of Alzoc III, cutting into its crust. These mines were equipped with mechanical conveyors to carry out the ore, but the Talz slave miners that worked there never emerged from the pits. They were worked until they were injured or died,<ref name="TBSB" /> a frequent occurrence as the mines had no medical care or safety precautions.<ref name="GMS" /> In order to replace deceased or incapacitated miners, the Imperials periodically pushed young Talz over the edge of the pits. Their thick fur was considered enough to limit the damage sustained from such falls.<ref name="TBSB" /> The mines were abandoned by the Imperials when they retreated from the planet.<ref name="EGtPM" />

===Empire Reborn outpost===
{{Main|Alzoc III Base}}
The Empire Reborn outpost was a broad multi-storied structure with a number of outlying towers around a small circular landing pad. In addition to this, it also contained at least two other interior hangar bays. It was protected by a large [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]] housed within a three story tall circular chamber. The outpost was manned by a number of Imperial officers and stormtroopers, as well as [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]]. At least one member of the Reborn was stationed there when Kyle Katarn infiltrated the outpost.<ref name="JKJO" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|If I have dreamed truly, it is a cool, wet world, with wide, rich jungles beneath a deep indigo sky.|Muftak's racial memory of his homeworld|<ref name="TME" />}}
[[File:AlzocIII_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|An orbital shot of Alzoc III displaying large amounts of greenery.]]
The Talz first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> but were not given a homeworld until ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', published by [[West End Games]] in [[June]] [[1989]].<ref name="GG4" /> The planet subsequently appeared in a number of other reference books, including the Essential Guides<ref name="EGtPM" /> and [[Wizards of the Coast]] products.<ref name="AA" /> The planet itself was first visited in the demo of ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'' (later included in the Nintendo GameCube and Xbox full versions of the game as an unlockable level),<ref name="JKJO" /> and was again visited in the video game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'',<ref name="EAW" /> its expansion [[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption|''Forces of Corruption'']]<ref name="FOC" /> and the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Republic Heroes]]''.<ref name="TCW:RH" /> However, the ''Star Wars: Empire at War'' mission involves the Empire defeating a large Rebel fleet at the planet, with the option of destroying the planet with the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. Accordingly, elements of this mission are non-[[canon]] as they conflict with existing continuity. The Alzoc III mission in ''Forces of Corruption'' is an optional side quest in the Zann Consortium campaign.<ref name="EAW" /> Alzoc III is also mentioned in the [[BioWare]]–[[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', and some of the Republic-allied Talz who appear on Hoth refer to their planet as one of the reasons they are comfortable on Hoth.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

As alluded to earlier in the Description section, in ''Play It Again, Figrin D'An: The Tale of Muftak and Kabe'' ([[August]] [[1995]]), from an early age the orphan Muftak experienced vivid dreams of his homeworld as a lush jungle world. His friend [[Momaw Nadon/Legends|Momaw Nadon]], an [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] botanist, assured him these were "[r]acial memories, no doubt, to guide you when you emerge from your cocoon."<ref name="TME" /> These dreams did not fit with the established terrain in ''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races''.<ref name="GG4" /> This difference was later [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] by [[Daniel Wallace]] in ''The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons'', where it was stated that Muftak "imagined" the terrain of the planet, and that "no one had the knowledge to correct him." The extent of the misconception that went uncorrected is not clear. It could be that the memories corresponded to an earlier time in the evolution of the Talz, and are no longer accurate. Alternatively, Muftak may have seen these plants outdoors.<ref name="EGtPM" /> It is known that some ice planets had different ecosystems within underground grottoes, such as Hoth (seen [[:File:Tauntauncave-woswfg.jpg|here]]),<ref name="Wildlife">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> and so the dreams could have been misinterpreted in this manner. The most recent orbital depiction of Alzoc III from the ''New Essential Guide to Alien Species'' ([[October]] [[2006]]) shows large swaths of green on the planet, also suggesting the planet may not be uniformly frozen.<ref name="GtAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>
